name: autoresearch-baseline decide(propose) → autoresearch-propose (iteration 1)
description: ADR-042 §Phase 2 redesign autoresearch pack. Fires when autoresearch-baseline terminates with decide(action=propose) — baseline has measured the reference value and stamped the run parameters onto the run entity via emit_autoresearch_baseline. Spawns the first autoresearch-propose loop. From here forward, rule 05 (continue) chains additional propose loops; this rule fires exactly once per autoresearch run.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.autoresearch-propose
on_enter.prompt:
AUTORESEARCH PROPOSE — iteration 1 of $entity.triple.autoresearch.cap.

The baseline at loop $entity.instance measured the reference value and stamped the run parameters on the run entity. Your job is to propose ONE concrete change to the surface that you hypothesise will lower the metric, apply it via bash, and hand off to execute.

Iteration 1 — call read_loop_result on $entity.instance (the baseline loop) for the parameters + the baseline measurement. The reason field carries: command, surface, cap, metric_parser, baseline_value, baseline_pass.

Iteration 2 — write your hypothesis to scratchpad. Be concrete: name the file(s) you intend to edit, the change pattern (delete N redundant fixtures, batch K parallel setups, swap library X for Y), and your prediction (qualitative — the empirical reviewer in execute will judge the actual value). Avoid:

- Changes outside the surface globs (the rule pre-filter does not enforce surface; the prompt does, and the reviewer's substance check will catch out-of-surface changes if they leak through).
- Changes that would break the pass gate (deleting tests, disabling assertions, adding t.Skip, //nolint). The execute phase verifies pass; a crash on first execute wastes an iteration.
- Multi-axis changes in one iteration. One hypothesis per iteration — the empirical compare only tells you whether the bundle improved, not which axis. Keep the diff narrow so the kept-vs-reverted signal is interpretable.

Iteration 3 — bash: apply your diff using whatever shell tools fit (sed -i, patch, awk, direct rewrite via cat > file). Stay within surface. Verify with `git diff --stat` that the changes are scoped as intended.

Iteration 4 — call decide(action="measure", reason="<hypothesis verbatim + diff summary + your surface-bounded edits>"). The execute phase reads your reason via read_loop_result; keep the substance in the reason field. The framework stamps coordinator.decision.next_action=measure on your loop entity; rule 03 fires and spawns autoresearch-execute.

If you genuinely cannot form a hypothesis (the baseline value is already at a hard floor, the surface is too narrow to permit any improvement, the metric is degenerate), decide(action="needs_clarification", reason="<specific reason no hypothesis is possible>") — recovery routes to coordinator.

Per ADR-041 addendum 2026-05-15: chain agents do not query the graph. Bash + read_loop_result are your only read channels.

metadata.fires_once_per_run: Rule 02 only fires when role=autoresearch-baseline; subsequent iterations fire rule 05 (role=coordinator, the run entity, length_lt cap). Both spawn autoresearch-propose; the iteration_index property differs (1 here, $length+1 in rule 05 via .length substitution).
metadata.lineage_threading: related_loops carries autoresearch-run (the run entity id, threaded via lineage chain) AND autoresearch-baseline (for first-iteration propose to access baseline measurement via read_loop_result). run-loop-entity-id is the spawn-time stable reference rule 04 will substitute against — sidesteps semstreams#159 race.
